function: Learned joint allocation of transmit power, radio bandwidth, subchannels and computation, with user association and MSP selection, across ground, aerial (UAV, HAPS) and LEO satellite links (pp. 9-10).
system: O-RAN TN-NTN: ground BSs, UAV/HAPS and LEO satellite serve 120 MUs; antenna gains only, no array, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated, 400-1200 MHz radio resources (pp. 7, 12-13).
method: Hierarchical multi-agent PPO (MAPPO), MLP actor and critic per agent with 128-64-32 hidden units; reinforcement learning, centralized training with decentralized execution (pp. 11-12).
data_channel: Custom simulator: path loss with small-scale fading, 120 MUs random in a 3 km x 3 km area; no standard channel model, dataset or measurement (pp. 6-7, 12).
test_conditions: Trained 10^4 episodes of 300 steps; results versus episodes, number of MUs, subchannels, bandwidth and meta-data size in the same simulator; no separate test scenario (pp. 12-15).
baselines: Randomized algorithm (non-learned); standard MADDPG and modified MADDPG (learned) (p. 13).
metrics: Average reward, energy consumption, QoE, latency, meta-distance, computation cost, resource utilization (pp. 13-15).
complexity: Big-O of MLP forward pass, centralized training over episodes, steps and agents, and per-step decentralized execution, Eqs. (28)-(30) (p. 12); no runtime reported.
q1_support: p. 7: "captures the power gain due to small-scale fading". The channel is a custom path-loss and fading model (Eq. 2, p. 6; Table III, p. 13); no 3GPP TR 38.811 or other standard model, and no measured data, is named.
q2_support: p. 14: "all algorithms demonstrated an increase in energy consumption with the number of MUs". Results are swept over MUs, subchannels, bandwidth and data size (pp. 14-15), but the paper never states that a trained policy is tested on a setting unseen in training, or how each setting is trained.
q3_support: p. 13: "we compare the performance of the proposed MAPPO algorithm with three benchmarks: the Randomized approach [38], the modified-MADDPG algorithm [39], and the standard MADDPG algorithm [40]". Randomized is non-learned; the MADDPG variants are earlier learned methods; compared on energy, latency, QoE, meta-distance and cost (pp. 14-15).
q4_support: p. 12: "The computational complexity for a single forward pass through the MLP of agent k is expressed as" O(sum of L_{n-1,k} L_{n,k} + L_{n,k} L_{n+1,k}), Eq. (28); Eqs. (29)-(30) give the training and per-step execution complexity.
q5_support: p. 12: "In our simulations, we used a core i7 server with a 2.4GHz Intel Xeon CPU and 32GB RAM". The environment is the authors' own simulator (Table III, p. 13); the paper gives no code or data link, no DOI and no public channel dataset.
notes: Included. Step 1: the learned policy chooses power, bandwidth and subchannels on aerial and satellite links jointly with association, computation and MSP selection, so above_phy does not exclude it. p. 10: 'allocated computation, transmission power, radio, and channel resources'; p. 9: 'a joint strategy for MSP selection and resource allocation, i.e., computation, power, and radio resources'. Area 6 (resource and power control in TN-NTN); NTN admits single-antenna links. Borderline for the reviewer: most actions are above the physical layer (association, MSP selection, computation, offloading). Abstract (p. 1) names 'centralized optimization approaches' as baselines, but p. 13 lists only Randomized, MADDPG and modified MADDPG. Tables I-III are images: Table III (p. 13) has no carrier frequency or channel model. The PDF text prints the episode count as 104, read as 10^4 from p. 13 'over 10,000 episodes'.
